title: Novum Bio — POC scoping: open-model shortlist & benchmarks
summary: POC scoping to pick an open-model shortlist for Novum Bio's document summarization + multi-lingual triage pipeline. Discussed success criteria (f1/rouge targets, latency), workload sizing (QPS, token distribution), benchmarks (end-to-end latency and quality), timeline (2-week benchmark, 8-week POC), infra constraints (HIPAA-ish data controls, VPC option), and Redwood deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Agreed on next steps: share security pack, price + capacity estimate, run baseline benchmarks with 3 models, schedule technical deep-dive next week.
topics: Model shortlist: Llama-2-13B, Mistral-Instruct, Falcon-40B, Mosaic-7B-cq
Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC)
Benchmarks: latency, cost, ROUGE/F1, hallucination rate
action_items: Samir Patel | Provide representative dataset samples (100 docs) | due: 2026-04-16
Evan Moore | Spin up benchmark harness + example prompts in Redwood test project | due: 2026-04-15
Priya Shah | Send security + SOC2 doc + KMS integration notes | due: 2026-04-13
Kelsey Wong | Confirm POC success criteria (acceptable latency and quality thresholds) | due: 2026-04-16
next_steps: Redwood to run three-model baseline (Llama 2 13B, Mistral Instruct, Falcon 40B) on sample set — results in 3 business days
Schedule technical deep-dive with infra team (Evan + Samir) next Wed 10am PT
Agree on POC start date: target week of 2026-04-26
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Priya Shah, Evan Moore (Redwood); Dr. Lena Torres, Samir Patel, Kelsey Wong (Novum Bio)
[00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Priya, account exec at Redwood. Evan's our SE, he'll go deep on models and bench.
[00:22] Dr. Lena Torres: Hi, Lena here. We built a pipeline to summarize research abstracts and route them by topic and language. We're looking at a POC to evaluate open models for quality and throughput.
[00:35] Samir Patel: Yeah, hi. Quick context: ~200 rps peak for short summaries, average input ~700 tokens, some up to 3k when they include methods. Sensitive-ish data — need data residency and audit logs.
[00:50] Evan Moore: Got it. That token distribution matters a lot for kernel selection and cache. For POC we usually size by peak qps and tail latency — what's your target latency?
[01:05] Kelsey Wong: Ideally sub 600ms per response at p95 for single-shot summarization; for long docs we can accept 1.5s. Cost is also important; we can't blow budget on 40B all the time.
[01:20] Priya Shah: Good. So success criteria — let's capture that. Kelsey, is p95 latency + quality threshold the main success metric? And any automated quality metric you want? ROUGE-L / BLEU are noisy for abstractive summaries but we can run ROUGE and a human eval sample.
[01:38] Kelsey Wong: Yeah, we were thinking ROUGE-L > 0.45 on our dev set and human eval accept rate > 85% for factuality. Also multi-lingual support: Spanish and Mandarin are prioritized after English.
[01:50] Dr. Lena Torres: And hallucination rate — if the model invents clinical claims, that's a hard fail.
[02:02] Evan Moore: Right, hallucination is tricky — we can include targeted sanity checks and prompt engineering in the bench. We'll also measure hallucination proxies like contradictions and factuality checks using our internal QA rules.
[02:18] Samir Patel: For throughput, think 200 rps peak, average 40 rps steady; batch-friendly workloads in the internal pipeline but some latency-sensitive endpoints.
[02:30] Priya Shah: On deployment modes: Redwood Hosted gives fastest onboarding but if you need VPC/private, Dedicated pools or Private deployment are options. Which is Novum's preference for POC?
[02:44] Dr. Lena Torres: For POC, hosted with data controls is fine, but if it looks promising we will move to dedicated with VPC/KMS. We need SOC2 and HIPAA language in the docs though.
[02:58] Priya Shah: We'll share SOC2 and KMS/HSM integration notes — Evan will attach those.
[03:05] Evan Moore: On model shortlist: based on your scientific domain and multilingual needs, I recommend we bench Llama-2-13B-instruct (open), Mistral-Instruct-7B (good instruction tuning), Falcon-40B-instruct (strong on English), and Mosaic-7B-cq as a low-cost baseline. We can also test quantized variants (Q4_0/ Q4_K_M) to measure tradeoffs.
[03:28] Samir Patel: Curious about Falcon — isn't Falcon 40B huge for us cost-wise?
[03:35] Evan Moore: It is. The idea is to run it as a quality upper bound. If Falcon shows only marginal gains vs Mistral or Llama-13B, we avoid it in production. Also, quantization can reduce memory and cost.
[03:50] Kelsey Wong: How about multilingual — Llama2 is decent, but we've seen Mistral struggles with Mandarin in our quick tests. Any recommendations?
[04:02] Evan Moore: Good point. We should include a Mandarin-specific prompt set. For Mandarin, some community models or fine-tuned checkpoints perform better; if base open models fail, we can propose small domain-tuning or retrieval-augmented prompting. We'll capture per-language ROUGE and a human pass rate.
[04:20] Dr. Lena Torres: Ok — and can Redwood run benchmarks for us? We want end-to-end numbers including tokenization overhead, KV cache impact for multi-turn, and prefix caching for similar abstracts.
[04:34] Priya Shah: Yes, Redwood can run the benchmark harness against your sample set in our test project. Evan: what's your typical bench run time?
[04:42] Evan Moore: With 1000 docs across three models, we can get initial numbers in 48–72 hours. We'll measure latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, per-1000-token cost estimate, and quality metrics.
[04:55] Samir Patel: Sounds good. We'll send representative samples — 100 initially, then scale to 1k.
[05:02] Kelsey Wong: Timeline — how long would the POC itself be? We're thinking 6–8 weeks with a go/no-go at week 4.
[05:12] Priya Shah: That aligns with our standard. Typical cadence: Week 0-1: bench + config; Week 2-3: pilot at low traffic; Week 4: quality review and decision; Week 5-8: scale & integration.
[05:25] Evan Moore: Also capture cost controls: auto-fallback to smaller models, routing by policy, and batching for high-throughput jobs. We'll include sample configs for batching and cache which should reduce unit cost a lot.
[05:40] Samir Patel: About data controls — are logs stored? We need audit logs and ability to disable retention for PII docs.
[05:50] Priya Shah: Yes, Redwood supports disabling retention, SSO/SAML, and KMS for key management. We'll include the security pack that details audit logs and retention toggles.
[06:05] Kelsey Wong: For benchmarks, please surface per-token cost and projected monthly spend assuming 200rps peak and 2M tokens/day. We want a range for hosted vs dedicated.
[06:20] Evan Moore: We'll include cost projection table — you can see cost per 1M tokens for each model and quantization variant. We'll also show break-even points for Dedicated reserved capacity.
[06:35] Dr. Lena Torres: Any gotchas with long inputs ~3k tokens? Does Redwood handle that efficiently?
[06:44] Evan Moore: Yes, runtime supports longer sequences, KV cache management and attention optimizations. For 3k sequences, memory and latency increase; we'll show perf numbers in the bench. For very long docs we sometimes chunk + retrieve/concat.
[06:58] Samir Patel: Should we plan to test retrieval-augmented pipelines? We have an internal vector DB and embeddings flow.
[07:06] Evan Moore: Absolutely. RAG can dramatically improve factuality; we can test an approach where we retrieve passages and then do an answer-generation step. That will be an extra bench variant.
[07:18] Priya Shah: Ok let's enumerate the bench variants: 1) baseline single-shot summarization per model; 2) quantized variant; 3) RAG variant with embeddings; 4) multi-lingual prompts (Spanish, Mandarin).
[07:35] Kelsey Wong: Sounds comprehensive. For success criteria, to be explicit: ROUGE-L > 0.45, human accept > 85%, hallucination < 3% across sampled set, p95 latency < 600ms for <1k token docs. Is that captured?
[07:52] Dr. Lena Torres: Yes please add hallucination threshold.
[07:55] Priya Shah: Noted. We'll include that in the POC doc.
[08:02] Samir Patel: On infra footprint, curious about GPU sizing. If we test 13B quantized at Q4_0 we can run many more concurrency on A10G-like instances, but 40B needs A100 class.
[08:15] Evan Moore: Correct. We'll provide instance maps: 7B/13B Q4 variants fit on 80–100GB pool more densely; 40B requires higher memory and is more expensive per token. We'll show throughput per GPU as part of the bench.
[08:30] Kelsey Wong: For multilingual, if Llama2 lags on Mandarin, what's the mitigation path? Fine-tune small on our corpus or use translation + summarization? Which is faster?
[08:42] Evan Moore: Quickest is translate-then-summarize but adds latency and translation fidelity issues. Fine-tuning a small 2-5k step cheap fine-tune or LoRA on Llama2 could improve quality and still be cost-effective. We'll outline both.
[08:58] Dr. Lena Torres: Do you have examples of scientific-domain fine-tunes?
[09:03] Evan Moore: We have several case notes internally and partner stories; I'll share anonymized snippets. For POC, we can do a small domain-adapt run in the bench if you provide labeled pairs.
[09:18] Samir Patel: Next, security review — we'll need the SOC2 report and data flow diagram for the hosted flow. Also confirm KMS for key wrapping and customer-managed keys for Private/Dedicated.
[09:30] Priya Shah: We'll attach SOC2 and KMS notes. For dedicated VPC, we support customer-managed keys and private links.
[09:40] Kelsey Wong: Great. Any concerns about model hallucinations creating regulatory issues for clinical claims?
[09:48] Evan Moore: That's why we include hallucination checks and RAG. Also run constrained generation templates and factuality classifiers as post-checks. We'll include those patterns in the engineering runbook.
[09:59] Dr. Lena Torres: For timeline, can we start bench next week?
[10:03] Priya Shah: Yes — we'll need the 100 doc sample by Friday. Evan will kick off bench once he has samples and prompts.
[10:12] Samir Patel: We'll also provide tokenization stats so you can pick ideal chunking.
[10:18] Evan Moore: Perfect. On success criteria again, to reiterate: quality + latency + hallucination thresholds, and cost estimates. We'll produce a decision sheet.
[10:28] Kelsey Wong: One more thing — any regulatory or compliance add-on costs for Private?
[10:34] Priya Shah: There can be additional license/support fees for Private deployments and on-prem bundles; we'll include a pricing estimate and optional SKUs.
[10:40] Dr. Lena Torres: Ok, let's recap and next steps.
[10:44] Priya Shah: Recap: Redwood to run 3-model baseline (Llama-2-13B, Mistral-Instruct-7B, Falcon-40B) plus Mosaic-7B baseline/quantized variants; measure latency p50/p95, cost per 1M tokens, ROUGE/human-eval, hallucination proxies; run multi-lingual tests for Spanish and Mandarin; include RAG variant. Deliverables in 48–72 hours for initial bench; fuller POC plan & pricing by next Tue.
[11:10] Samir Patel: Sounds good, thanks.
[11:15] Kelsey Wong: Thanks everyone.
[11:18] Priya Shah: I'll send notes, security pack, and set up the benchmark project. Evan will reach out to Samir for creds and dataset.
[11:28] End of call.
